name: HPLC Purity Reporting Checklist and Coding Scheme for Research Peptides
scope: Fields that must accompany a chromatographic purity claim for the number to be interpretable by a third party.

fields.typical_value: C18, 4.6 x 250 mm, 5 um (or stated equivalent)
fields.why_it_matters: Without it, retention and selectivity cannot be compared between laboratories.

fields.typical_value: 0.1% TFA in water / 0.1% TFA in acetonitrile
fields.why_it_matters: Ion-pairing choice shifts elution order; different systems are not interchangeable.
A percentage without a ramp time is not a method.
Amide absorbance varies by sequence; a different wavelength changes the reported purity.
Both affect resolution and therefore the integration baseline.
Overloaded injections distort area-% in both directions.
The reporting threshold determines the number that gets quoted.
Unstated limits make two '99%' claims incomparable.
Without suitability data the run is not demonstrably valid.

comparability_rules: Two purity values are comparable only if column chemistry, wavelength, gradient, and reporting threshold are identical.
Area-% is not content: content requires an independent assay (mass balance, nitrogen, or quantitative NMR).
A single main-peak percentage does not describe the impurity profile; the reporting limit sets what is visible.
Cumulative impurity reporting ('other peaks total') is more informative than the main-peak figure alone.
common_failure_modes: Wavelength omitted, then two suppliers report different purities for the same material.
Gradient stated as a final percentage without a ramp time.
Purity quoted to 0.1% while the reporting limit is 1.0%.
Different lots compared across two different methods.
